subject: Request: prioritize Acme feature set for enterprise close (model pinning + per-customer cache)
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: prioritize Acme feature set for enterprise close (model pinning + per-customer cache)

Team — looping you in on a high-priority opportunity. Acme Financial (HS-87432) is asking for two product items as gating items for an SSO+Private deployment close: 1) model-variant pinning per-customer (they need deterministic model behavior for audits) and 2) per-customer prefix/KV cache isolation (so keys aren't shared across tenants). They attached a one-page requirements doc (Acme_MAAP_Requirements.pdf).

Why this matters: this is a $1.2M ARR expansion (see deal id above). The customer is sensitive to compliance and expects these items to be in place before signing. They have an aggressive timeline: pilot in 6 weeks, prod in 12.

Ask: can Product/Eng evaluate a prioritized spike for these two capabilities and give rough ETA / risk? If immediate engineering work is unlikely, what's the minimal workaround we can offer (config/ops control, extra logging, temporary model-version freeze) to keep the deal moving?

I know this overlaps with Private deployment work (KMS/SSO), but the customer called out deterministic model selection and strict KV isolation as separate contractual clauses.

Next steps I propose:
- Quick sync today if possible (15-20m)
- If OK, create an ENG ticket and scope a 2-week spike with acceptance criteria (customer audit checklist).

Thanks — Dev

--
Dev Patel
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments (2): Acme_MAAP_Requirements.pdf (application/pdf), acme_sla_checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.ms-excel)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: prioritize Acme feature set for enterprise close (model pinning + per-customer cache)

Thanks Dev — good context. High-level thoughts from infra/product:

1) Model-variant pinning: we can expose a per-customer routing rule that ties a customer to a model-version id. Implementation paths:
  - Short term (1-2 weeks spike): add routing metadata + enforcement at the smart-router layer; model selection would be a config-only change (no model retrain). Risk: needs testing for cache compatibility and fallback behavior.
  - Mid term (4-8 weeks): persist pinning in our control plane and add UI/API to manage mappings with audit logs.

2) Per-customer cache isolation: this is trickier. Our KV/prefix caching is optimized for cross-tenant reuse. To fully isolate keys per customer we can namespace caches by tenant id (engineering work to change cache keys + storage routing).
  - Spike estimate: 2 weeks to prove concept on staging (ENG-4921).
  - Full rollout: 6-10 weeks including perf testing and rollback strategies.

Workarounds to propose to Acme:
- Dedicated cache pool on Dedicated instances (if they take a Dedicated seat we can allocate separate pools) — faster but higher cost.
- Enforce model pinning + aggressive TTLs on shared cache to reduce cross-tenant leakage risk.

Questions:
- Is Acme willing to accept a staged approach (pinning first, cache isolation later)?
- Does their compliance team require audit logs for pinning changes? If so, we should include that in acceptance criteria.

I'll spin up ENG-4921 and propose acceptance criteria. If you can confirm customer flexibility on staging, I can prioritize a 2-week spike.

—Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product, Serving Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: prioritize Acme feature set for enterprise close (model pinning + per-customer cache)

FWIW from CS & legal intake: Acme's security team has two hard requirements: (A) demonstrable model determinism during audit windows (they want deterministic outputs for a fixed prompt corpus) and (B) cryptographic separation of customer data (they prefer separate key spaces). They explicitly noted they will not move to prod until (A) is testable and (B) is either in place or they accept a monitored Dedicated workaround.

They are open to "pinning + staged cache isolation" but only if we can commit to audit evidence for the first milestone. The customer also signaled budget for an integration fee if we can accelerate.

I'll share the exact language they sent below (redacted):

"On Wed, Mar 18, 2026 at 08:40 AM Lisa Bowman <lisa.bowman@acme-fin.com> wrote:

> We need determinism for compliance audits and clear separation of data. If Redwood can provide a path with measurable acceptance tests within 6 weeks for pilot, we'll expedite approvals.
> 
> Regards,
> Lisa


We should capture specific acceptance criteria (e.g., deterministic outputs on a 50-prompt audit set, cache namespace per-tenant demonstrated on staging). Happy to run the compliance validation with Acme once we have a spike build.

—Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Enterprise Accounts
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Lisa Bowman <lisa.bowman@acme-fin.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: prioritize Acme feature set for enterprise close (model pinning + per-customer cache)

Dev — thanks for the intro. To be explicit: our compliance team needs a reproducible test that demonstrates the same outputs for a canonical prompt set when pinned to a model-version. For cache isolation, we need assurance that at-rest keys are not shared. We prefer the Dedicated cache option if that makes delivery faster.

We are willing to sign the MSA contingent on delivery milestones and to pay an acceleration fee if Redwood can commit resources immediately. Can you confirm a sync later today to align on scope?

Best,
Lisa Bowman
Director of Platform Risk, Acme Financial
lisa.bowman@acme-fin.com

--

Thanks Lisa (and team) — I'll take ownership for a scoped spike. Plan:

1) Create ENG-4921: spike to add per-customer model pinning enforcement in router + acceptance tests (deterministic 50-prompt suite). 2-week spike starting Mon 3/22.
2) Evaluate Dedicated cache as an expedited mitigation; if Acme funds acceleration we can provision a dedicated pool and run the namespace change in parallel (goal: pilot in 6 weeks).
3) Deliverables: spike branch, automated acceptance tests, staging demo run with Acme's audit corpus, and a roll-forward plan for full rollout.

I'll scope the spike and post an initial implementation plan to the Jira ticket by EOD. Schedule: let's do a 20-minute alignment call today at 4pm PT.

Link to ticket: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/ENG-4921

—Karthik
